title: Accelerating Storage-based Training for Graph Neural Networks

problem.claim: Storage-based GNN training must handle web-scale graphs on a single machine using external storage.

gap.claim: Existing storage-based GNN training methods suffer from a severe data-preparation bottleneck because they overlook the challenge of handling many small storage I/Os.

contributions.claim: AGNES is a storage-based GNN training framework that uses block-wise storage I/O processing to utilize the I/O bandwidth of high-performance storage devices.
AGNES uses hyperbatch-based processing to improve the efficiency of each storage I/O based on real-world graph characteristics.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present AGNES as a novel storage-based GNN training framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on five real-world graphs are reported to show that AGNES consistently outperforms four state-of-the-art methods.
AGNES is reported to be up to 4.1× faster than the best competitor.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNNs have achieved breakthroughs in real-world downstream tasks because of their expressive power.
Growing graph scale has motivated storage-based GNN training with external storage on a single machine.
Existing methods face a severe data-preparation bottleneck from many small storage I/Os.
AGNES addresses the bottleneck with block-wise storage I/O processing and hyperbatch-based processing.
The authors report consistent gains over four state-of-the-art methods on five real-world graphs, reaching up to 4.1× speedup over the best competitor.

source_observation.claim: A large number of small storage I/Os can become a critical data-preparation bottleneck in storage-based GNN training.

interpretation.claim: Systems operating over external storage should optimize I/O granularity and organization, not only aggregate storage bandwidth.

application.claim: For web-scale graph training on a single machine, consider block-wise I/O processing and workload-aware batching strategies.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether these strategies generalize beyond the reported real-world graph workloads or storage configurations.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the five graphs, their sizes, or graph characteristics.
The storage hardware, software configuration, workload settings, and evaluation metrics are unspecified.
The abstract does not report ablations separating the effects of block-wise I/O processing and hyperbatch-based processing.
